dismissed_hits.reason: Its C4 witness refutes a bound on the number of central vertices, not a bound on radius. The retained clause applies only to forest components of G-S after S is an FVS; such components have radius at most 3.
It concerns singleton vertex separators in non-bipartite unichord-free graphs and has no bearing on induced even cycles or forest components after deleting an FVS.
It refutes a recursive planarity criterion involving cycle segments; the draft makes no planarity or segment-decomposition inference.

It concerns using the pre-reduction graph size in an approximation exponent after enlarging an input. Here the 8-approximation is constructed directly on the original graph, and O(8^k n^8) also uses that same input size.
It refutes a graph-coloring-to-river-crossing reduction; neither crossing schedules nor coloring partitions occur in the draft.
It refutes uniqueness of an extremal C5-free planar graph. The draft claims neither planarity nor uniqueness of an extremal graph.
It concerns an unrelated unit-distance conjecture and supplies no counterexample to any graph statement or algorithm used here.
It exposes a missing k! in factorial moments. The draft uses no probabilistic moments or ordered-versus-unordered tuple conversion.
It concerns extremal numbers of forbidden families. Here all three short-cycle types are retained and hit; the argument does not replace their conjunction by a single allegedly hardest obstruction.
It concerns directed transitive closure and the failure of undirected spanning-tree reasoning for directed reachability. Every graph and path used here is undirected.
It refutes an edge-cut block decomposition. The draft makes no claim about bonds or decomposing cuts into component-pair blocks.

results.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
results.proof_sketch: If G-S contains a cycle, choose a shortest one. It is chordless, hence induced in G. Bipartiteness makes its length even. An induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices, impossible; thus the cycle is C4, C6, or C8. The converse is immediate, so hitting those induced cycles is equivalent to being an FVS. Once S is an FVS, every component of G-S is a tree. A tree of diameter at least 7 contains an induced eight-vertex path, so its diameter is at most 6 and its radius at most 3. If S is inclusion-minimal and x∈S, then G-(S minus {x}) has a cycle. Since G-S is a forest, that cycle uses x, and deleting x from it leaves a path in one component of G-S between two distinct neighbors of x.

results.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
results.proof_sketch: Enumerate all vertex subsets of sizes 4, 6, and 8 and retain those whose induced graph is exactly a cycle. By the preceding equivalence, the resulting rank-at-most-eight hypergraph has exactly the feedback vertex sets as its transversals. For the decision problem, select an unhit hyperedge and branch on deleting each of its at most eight vertices, giving O(8^k n^8) time and exhaustive coverage. For approximation, greedily construct a maximal family of vertex-disjoint listed cycles and return their union U. Maximality makes U a transversal and hence an FVS. If the family has p cycles, every FVS contains at least one vertex from each, so OPT≥p, while |U|≤8p≤8OPT.

results.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
results.proof_sketch: An exact finite enumeration gives the following lemma: no C4-free P8-free bipartite graph contains a simple path on 15 vertices. Fixing a required path's vertex order forces every allowable chord to join opposite index parities. Introducing vertices in order and rejecting exactly those extensions that create a C4 or an induced P8 gives survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. Any hypothetical 15-vertex path would induce one of these exhaustively considered ordered graphs. Now run an undirected DFS forest. Every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints, and each root-to-leaf path has at most 14 vertices. For each DFS vertex, the bag consisting of it and all its ancestors yields a tree decomposition: an edge shares the descendant endpoint's bag, and bags containing a fixed vertex form its descendant subtree. Thus the width is at most 13. A fixed-width forest-connectivity dynamic program computes minimum FVS in polynomial time.

results.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
results.proof_sketch: Within P8-free bipartite graphs, iterative deepening branches on the four vertices of an uncovered induced C4; at depth r it finds a minimum C4-transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. Then G-X is C4-free and remains P8-free and bipartite, so the previous claim gives a constructible width-13 decomposition. Add X to every bag, obtaining width at most r+13. On a nice decomposition, record the deleted bag vertices and the connectivity partition induced by retained partial-forest vertices; introduce-edge and join transitions reject precisely combinations that close a cycle. There are 2^{O(r log r)} states per bag. Minimizing deletion cost therefore computes an exact FVS within the claimed total bound.

results.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
results.proof_sketch: For the half-graph H_n with a_i b_j iff i≤j, neighborhoods are strictly nested on each side, so there are no false twins; it is 2K2-free and hence P5-free. Keeping all B and a_{n-1},a_n is C4-free, while if i<j are the two least retained A-indices, C4-freeness permits at most one retained b_l with l≥j, yielding at most n+2 retained vertices and thus transversal number n-2. For the theta graph formed by m internally disjoint length-three u-v paths, deleting any vertex leaves it connected, every cycle has length six, and every induced path has at most six vertices; it is therefore 2-connected, C4-free, P8-free, and has 2m+2 vertices. Finally, K_{3,3} is P4-free; its minimum FVS has size 2, but assigning 1/4 to every vertex satisfies each induced-C4 constraint with total 3/2, proving nonintegrality.

final_writeup:
The target asks for a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on all P8-free bipartite graphs. The arguments below give verified structural and algorithmic partial progress, but they do not establish that full result.

Let G be P8-free and bipartite. A set S is an FVS exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. If G-S has a cycle, a shortest such cycle is chordless and therefore induced in G. Its length is even; if it were at least 10, eight consecutive cycle vertices would induce P8. Conversely, an FVS meets every cycle. Once S is an FVS, each component of G-S is a tree of diameter at most 6 and hence radius at most 3. If S is inclusion-minimal, then for each x∈S, restoring x creates a cycle; deleting x from that cycle gives a path between two distinct neighbors of x in one component of G-S.

This equivalence gives two direct algorithms. Enumerate all induced cycles on 4, 6, or 8 vertices, viewing their vertex sets as a rank-eight hypergraph. Branching on all vertices of an uncovered hyperedge decides whether an FVS of size at most k exists in O(8^k n^8) time. A maximal collection of vertex-disjoint listed cycles gives an 8-approximation: its union is a transversal by maximality, and if there are p cycles, every FVS has size at least p whereas the union has size at most 8p.

There is also a polynomial subclass. Exact finite enumeration shows that a C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has no simple path on 15 vertices. Run a DFS forest, so disconnected inputs are handled componentwise. Every graph edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints, and every root-to-leaf path has at most 14 vertices. Bags consisting of each DFS vertex together with all its ancestors form a tree decomposition of width at most 13. Thus a fixed-width connectivity-partition dynamic program computes a minimum FVS in polynomial time on the C4-free subclass.

More generally, let r be the minimum size of a C4-transversal. Branching on an uncovered C4 finds such a transversal X in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. A width-13 decomposition of G-X becomes a width-(r+13) decomposition of G after X is added to every bag. The usual FVS dynamic program, whose states specify deleted bag vertices and a connectivity partition of retained vertices, has 2^{O(r log r)} states per bag. This yields an exact 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)} algorithm.

These results do not collapse to a polynomial algorithm on the whole class. Half-graphs are already P5-free, have no false twins, and have unbounded C4-transversal number. Theta graphs made of arbitrarily many internally disjoint length-three paths between two terminals are 2-connected, C4-free, P8-free, and have unbounded order. The short-cycle covering LP is nonintegral even on K_{3,3}: the integral optimum is 2, while value 1/4 on every vertex is feasible with objective 3/2.

Accordingly, target coverage remains partial. The parameterized algorithm is exponential in k, the bounded-treewidth algorithm assumes C4-freeness, and the r-parameter algorithm is exponential in a parameter that is unbounded on the target class. No complete polynomial-time algorithm for all P8-free bipartite graphs is established here.
